question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Explorer — Sea Route/Achievement]
options: Vasco da Gama — First European to reach India by sea via the Cape of Good Hope
Christopher Columbus — Reached the Caribbean islands in 1492 believing it to be the East Indies
Ferdinand Magellan — Led the first expedition to circumnavigate the globe
Bartholomeu Dias — First European to sail around the Cape of Good Hope and reach Calicut on the Indian coast
wrong_fact: Bartholomeu Dias sailed around the Cape of Good Hope in 1488 but he did NOT reach Calicut or the Indian coast — his crew forced him to turn back at Kwaaihoek (present-day South Africa). It was Vasco da Gama who later reached Calicut (1498).
explanation: Bartholomeu Dias (1488) rounded the Cape of Good Hope (initially called the Cape of Storms) and proved a sea route to Asia was possible, but his voyage ended at the Great Fish River/Kwaaihoek and he never reached India. Vasco da Gama (1498) was the first to complete the full voyage to Calicut. The other three options are correctly matched: Columbus reached the Caribbean (1492), Magellan's expedition circumnavigated the globe (1519–1522), and Vasco da Gama reached India via the Cape of Good Hope.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Portuguese Expedition — Port/Region Established or Reached]
options: Pedro Álvares Cabral (1500) — Brazil (accidentally landed while attempting to reach India)
Vasco da Gama (1498) — Calicut (Kozhikode) on the Malabar Coast of India
Alfonso de Albuquerque (1510) — Goa (captured from the Bijapur Sultanate)
Bartolomeu Dias (1488) — Mozambique and Malindi on the East African Coast
wrong_fact: Bartolomeu Dias (1488) rounded the Cape of Good Hope but did NOT reach Mozambique or Malindi — those East African ports were visited by Vasco da Gama during his 1498 voyage to India. Dias turned back near the Great Fish River.
explanation: Vasco da Gama's 1498 voyage took him along the East African coast stopping at Mozambique and Malindi (Kenya) before crossing the Indian Ocean to Calicut. Dias in 1488 only rounded the Cape of Good Hope and could not proceed further. Pedro Cabral's accidental discovery of Brazil (1500) is correctly matched, as is Albuquerque's capture of Goa (1510) from Adil Shah of Bijapur.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Geographical Concept / Region — Correct Historical Association during Age of Discovery]
options: Tordesillas Line (1494) — Divided the newly discovered world between Portugal (east) and Spain (west)
Strait of Malacca — Critical choke point controlled by Portuguese after 1511, linking Indian Ocean to the South China Sea
Hormuz — Strategic Persian Gulf island captured by Portuguese in 1515 to control the spice and silk trade routes
Cape Verde Islands — Located in the South Atlantic off the coast of West Africa; served as Spanish staging point for Pacific voyages
wrong_fact: Cape Verde Islands are located off the coast of West Africa in the North Atlantic, not the South Atlantic. More critically, they were a Portuguese territory (discovered 1456–60 under Portuguese patronage), NOT a Spanish staging point. They served as a key resupply base for Portuguese voyages to Africa and India.
explanation: Cape Verde Islands lie roughly 570 km off the coast of Senegal/Mauritania in the North Atlantic and were a Portuguese colony, not Spanish. They were a crucial resupply stop for Portuguese explorations. The other options are correctly matched: the Treaty of Tordesillas (1494) did divide newly discovered lands between Portugal and Spain; Malacca was captured by Albuquerque in 1511 and controlled the sea lane between the Indian Ocean and South China Sea; Hormuz was captured by Albuquerque in 1515 giving Portugal control over Persian Gulf trade.
